subject: maths
title: Word Problems and Money: Add, Take Away and Count Coins
seo_title: Year 1 Word Problems and Money Worksheets: Australian Coins, Free with Answer Key
standard_text: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving additive situations including simple money transactions; represent the situations with diagrams, physical and virtual materials, and use calculation strategies to solve the problem
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: picture story problems within 20, how many more, Australian coins (size is not value), counting small amounts of coins and simple buying at the class shop and canteen. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Picture the story. Do some come or go? Then add or take away.
key_sub: For “how many more”, line them up and count the extra ones. With coins, read the number, not the size, and count the value of each coin: 20c, 30c, 35c.
body_html:
Picture the story

Read the story. Ask: what happens? Do some come, or do some go away? Draw it. Then add or take away.

How many more?

Line up the two rows. Match them one to one. The extra ones are the answer.

Count on

Isla needs 10 stickers. She has 7. How many more does she need?

Count on from 7: 8, 9, 10. That is 3 jumps.

Answer: 3 more stickers

Australian coins

Our coins are 5c, 10c, 20c, 50c, $1 and $2. c means cents. $ means dollars. The $1 and $2 coins are gold.

Size is not value. The 50c coin is the biggest. The $2 coin is small, but it is worth the most. Read the number on the coin.

Count coins, biggest value first

Start with the coin worth the most. Then count on.

Buying

An apple costs 50c. Which coins can you use?

20c + 20c = 40c. 40c + 10c = 50c.

Answer: 20c, 20c and 10c

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when some go awayAsk: do they come or go? If they go, take away.
Adding for “how many more”Line them up. Count the extra ones: 8 − 5 = 3.
3 coins, so 3cAdd the value of each coin: 20c, 30c, 35c.
The 50c coin is biggest, so it is worth the mostRead the number: $2 is worth the most.
Mixing up $2 and 20c$ means dollars. c means cents. $2 is much more than 20c.

faq.q: What word problems do Year 1 students solve in Australia?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum (AC9M1N05), Year 1 students solve adding and taking-away problems, including simple buying with money. They show the story with pictures, objects or drawings, then add or subtract.

faq.q: Which coins does my Year 1 child need to know?
faq.a: The Australian coins are 5c, 10c, 20c, 50c, $1 and $2. Children read the number on each coin and count small amounts, such as 20c + 10c + 5c = 35c.

faq.q: Why is the 50c coin bigger than the $2 coin?
faq.a: The size of a coin does not show its value. The 50c coin is the biggest, but the small gold $2 coin is worth the most, so children should read the number.

faq.q: How can I help my child with “how many more” questions?
faq.a: Line up two rows of objects and match them one to one. The extra objects are the answer, so 8 stickers and 5 stickers means 3 more.

items.q: Amelia has a tower of 3 blocks. She adds 2 more. How many blocks are there now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. Start at 3 and count on 2: 4, 5. 3 + 2 = 5.

items.q: 6 fish were in the rock pool. 2 swam away. How many fish are left?
items.e: Some went away, so take away. Count the ones not crossed out. 6 − 2 = 4. Do not add.

items.q: There are 4 Anzac biscuits on a plate. Dad bakes 3 more. How many biscuits are there now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. Start at 4 and count on 3: 5, 6, 7. 4 + 3 = 7.

items.q: 8 cars were in the car park. 3 drove away. How many cars are left?
items.e: Some went away, so take away. Count the ones not crossed out. 8 − 3 = 5. Do not add.
Some more came, so add. Start at 5 and count on 4: 6, 7, 8, 9. 5 + 4 = 9.

items.q: In the sport shed there are 6 red balls and 3 blue balls. How many balls are there in all?
items.e: Put the two groups together, so add. Start with the bigger number, 6. Count on 3: 7, 8, 9. 6 + 3 = 9.

items.q: Grace had 9 balloons. 5 popped. How many balloons are left?
items.e: Some went away, so take away. Count the ones not crossed out. 9 − 5 = 4. Do not add.

items.q: Sienna planted 6 flowers. Then she planted 3 more. How many flowers are there now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. Start at 6 and count on 3: 7, 8, 9. 6 + 3 = 9.

items.e: Some went away, so take away. Count the ones not crossed out. 10 − 4 = 6. Do not add.

items.e: Some more came, so add. Start at 7 and count on 5: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. 7 + 5 = 12.

items.e: Some more came, so add. Start at 8 and count on 5: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. 8 + 5 = 13.
Some went away, so take away. Count the ones not crossed out. 13 − 5 = 8. Do not add.

items.e: Some more came, so add. Start at 8 and count on 7: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. 8 + 7 = 15.

items.q: Mia has 5 blocks. William has 3 blocks. How many more blocks does Mia have than William?
items.e: Match them one to one. 2 of Mia’s blocks have no match. 5 − 3 = 2. Do not add.

items.q: Jack has 8 toy cars. Mei has 5 toy cars. How many more cars does Jack have than Mei?

items.e: Match them one to one. 4 of William’s biscuits have no match. 9 − 5 = 4. Do not add.

items.e: Match them one to one. 2 of Aarav’s balls have no match. 8 − 6 = 2. Do not add.
Count on from 6 to 10: 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 4. Or count the empty spaces. 6 + 4 = 10.

items.q: Ruby wants to plant 10 flowers. She has planted 7. How many more flowers does she need to plant?
items.e: Count on from 7 to 10: 8, 9, 10. That is 3. Or count the empty spaces. 7 + 3 = 10.

items.e: Count on from 4 to 10: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 6. Or count the empty spaces. 4 + 6 = 10.

items.q: The fruit box holds 10 apples. Matilda has put in 8. How many more apples fit in the box?
items.e: Count on from 8 to 10: 9, 10. That is 2. Or count the empty spaces. 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Kai caught 14 fish off the jetty. Cooper caught 9. How many more fish did Kai catch than Cooper?

items.q: Harper picked 16 flowers. Kai picked 8 flowers. How many more flowers did Harper pick than Kai?
items.e: Count on from 8 to 16: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. That is 8. 16 − 8 = 8. Do not add.

items.q: Matilda has 13 toy cars. Kai has 7 toy cars. How many more cars does Matilda have than Kai?
items.e: Count on from 7 to 13: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 6. 13 − 7 = 6. Do not add.

items.q: Harper saw 15 ducks at the dam. Mei saw 11 ducks. How many fewer ducks did Mei see than Harper?
items.e: Count on from 11 to 15: 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 4. 15 − 11 = 4. Do not add.
Count on from 11 to 18: 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18. That is 7. 18 − 11 = 7. Do not add.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: The coin says 5c. The c means cents. It is worth 5c. It is our smallest coin.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: The coin says 10c. It is worth 10c (10 cents). $10 is a note.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: The coin says 20c. It is worth 20c (20 cents). $2 is a gold coin.

items.q: How much is this coin worth?
items.e: This coin has 12 sides. It says 50c. It is worth 50c (50 cents).

items.q: How much is this gold coin worth?
items.e: This gold coin says $1. It is worth $1 (one dollar). The $ sign means dollars.

items.q: How much is this gold coin worth?
items.e: This small gold coin says $2. It is worth $2 (two dollars), not 20c.

items.q: How much is this note worth?
items.e: The note says $5. It is worth $5 (five dollars).

items.q: Which coin has 12 sides?
items.e: The 50c coin has 12 sides. The other coins are round.

items.q: Which two coins are gold?
items.e: The $1 and $2 coins are gold. The cents coins are silver.

items.q: How do you write 20 cents?
items.e: Write the number, then c for cents: 20c. $20 would be 20 dollars.

items.q: How do you write 2 dollars?
items.e: Write the $ sign first, then the number: $2. 20c would be 20 cents.

items.q: The $1 coin is bigger than the $2 coin. Which coin is worth more?
items.e: Size does not tell you the value. Read the number. $2 is more than $1, so the $2 coin is worth more.

items.q: The 50c coin is bigger than the $1 coin. Which coin is worth more?
items.e: $1 is 100 cents. 100c is more than 50c. So the $1 coin is worth more, even though it is smaller.

items.q: Matilda has a 20c coin. Chloe has a $2 coin. Who has more money?
items.e: The 20c coin is bigger, but $2 is worth more than 20c. Chloe has more money.

items.q: Which coin is worth the most?
items.e: A is the $2 coin. It is worth the most. The 50c coin is the biggest, but it is only worth 50 cents.

items.q: Which coin is worth the least?
items.e: C is the 5c coin. 5 cents is the least. The $2 coin is small, but it is worth a lot.

items.q: Which coin is worth the most?
items.e: The $2 coin is worth the most, even though it is small. The 50c coin is the biggest, but it is worth less.
50c and 50c make 100c. 100c is the same as $1.

items.q: Two 10c coins are worth the same as which coin?
items.e: 10c and 10c make 20c. One 20c coin is worth the same.

items.q: Put these coins in order. Start with the least.
items.e: Cents come first: 20c, then 50c. Then dollars: $1, then $2. The order is 20c, 50c, $1, $2. Do not order them by size.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each coin is 10c. Count in 10s: 10c, 20c. That is 20c. There are 2 coins, but they are worth 20c.

items.q: Mia has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Each coin is 5c. Count in 5s: 5c, 10c, 15c. That is 15c. There are 3 coins, but they are worth 15c.

items.q: Mei finds these coins in her pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Each coin is 10c. Count in 10s: 10c, 20c, 30c. That is 30c. There are 3 coins, but they are worth 30c.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each coin is 20c. Count in 20s: 20c, 40c. That is 40c. There are 2 coins, but they are worth 40c.

items.q: Chloe puts these coins in her money box. How much is that?
items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 10c, 15c. That is 15c. There are 2 coins, but they are worth 15c.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 10c, 20c, 25c. That is 25c. There are 3 coins, but they are worth 25c.

items.q: Grace has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 20c, 30c. That is 30c. There are 2 coins, but they are worth 30c.

items.q: Sienna finds these coins in her pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 20c, 25c. That is 25c. There are 2 coins, but they are worth 25c.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each coin is 10c. Count in 10s: 10c, 20c, 30c, 40c. That is 40c. There are 4 coins, but they are worth 40c.

items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 20c, 30c, 35c. That is 35c. There are 3 coins, but they are worth 35c.

items.q: Ethan has these coins. How much does he have?
items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 50c, 60c. That is 60c. There are 2 coins, but they are worth 60c.

items.q: Isla finds these coins in her pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 50c, 70c. That is 70c. There are 2 coins, but they are worth 70c.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Put the coins in order, the most first. Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 20c, 30c, 40c, 45c. That is 45c. There are 4 coins, but they are worth 45c.

items.q: Zara puts these coins in her money box. How much is that?
items.e: Put the coins in order, the most first. Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 50c, 70c, 75c. That is 75c. There are 3 coins, but they are worth 75c.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Put the coins in order, the most first. Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: 10c, 15c, 20c. That is 20c. There are 3 coins, but they are worth 20c.
Each coin is 50c. Count in 50s: 50c, $1. That is $1. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: William finds these coins in his pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Each coin is $1. Count in 1s: $1, $2. That is $2. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: $2, $3. That is $3. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: Jack puts these coins in his money box. How much is that?
items.e: Start with the coin worth the most. Count on: $2, $4, $5. That is $5. Count the value of each coin, not the number of coins.

items.q: An apple costs 50c. Cooper has a 50c coin. Can he buy the apple?
items.e: The coin is worth 50c. The apple costs 50c. So yes, it is just right.

items.q: A pencil costs 30c. Ruby has a 20c coin. Can she buy the pencil?
items.e: 20c is less than 30c. So no. Ruby needs 10c more.

items.q: A sticker costs 20c. Lachlan has three 10c coins. Can he buy the sticker?
items.e: Count in tens: 10c, 20c, 30c. 30c is more than 20c, so yes. Count the value, not the coins.

items.q: A juice costs $2. Matilda has a $1 coin. Can she buy the juice?
items.e: The $1 coin is bigger, but it is worth less. $1 is less than $2, so no.

items.q: An apple costs 50c. Which coins make 50c?
A koala sticker costs 25c. Which coins make 25c?
items.e: 20c and 5c more is 25c. So 20c and 5c make 25c.

items.q: At the class shop, Amelia buys a pencil and a sticker. How much does she pay?
items.e: Buying two things, so add. 30c + 20c: count on in tens from 30c: 40c, 50c. That is 50c. 10c is what you get if you take away.

items.q: At the class shop, Mia buys a banana and a sticker. How much does she pay?
items.e: 40c + 20c: count on in tens from 40c: 50c, 60c. That is 60c.

items.q: Mei has 40c. She buys a pencil. How much money does she have left?
items.e: Mei spends money, so take away. Count on from 30c to 40c: 10c more. 40c − 30c = 10c.

items.q: Leo has 30c. How much more does he need to buy the apple?
items.e: Count on from 30c to 50c: 40c, 50c. That is 2 tens, so 20c more. Do not add.

items.q: Chloe buys 2 stickers. How much does she pay?
items.e: Each sticker is 20c. 20c + 20c = 40c. 22c adds the 2 to 20. 4c forgets that 2 tens is 20c.

items.q: Which two things cost 70c in all?
items.e: Apple 50c + sticker 20c = 70c. The answer is the apple and the sticker.

items.q: At the canteen, Kai buys an icy pole and a juice. How much does he pay?
items.e: Buying both, so add. $3 + $2 = $5. $1 is what you get if you take away.

items.q: Grace has $5. She buys an icy pole for $2. How much does she have left?
items.e: She spends $2, so take away. $5 − $2 = $3. Count back from 5: 4, 3.

items.q: Mum gives Sienna a $2 coin and two $1 coins. How much money is that?
items.e: Start with $2. Count on $1, $1: $3, $4. That is $4. There are 3 coins, but they are worth $4.

items.q: Aarav has four $2 coins. How much money does he have?
items.e: Count in twos: $2, $4, $6, $8. That is $8. $4 counts the coins, not their value.

items.q: A sausage sizzle costs $3. Noah buys 2. How much does he pay?
items.e: 2 lots of $3: $3 + $3 = $6. $5 adds 3 and 2, but Noah buys 2 lots of $3.

items.q: A koala toy costs $10. Charlotte has $6. How much more does she need?
items.e: Count on from $6 to $10: $7, $8, $9, $10. That is $4 more. Do not add: $16 is too much.

items.q: Amelia has 30c. Zara has 50c. How much more money does Zara have?
items.e: Count on from 30c to 50c: 40c, 50c. That is 20c more. Zara has 1 coin, but it is worth more.

items.q: Ethan has $9. He spends $5 at the school fete. How much does he have left?
items.e: He spends money, so take away. $9 − $5 = $4. Count on from $5 to $9: $6, $7, $8, $9. That is 4.
